# Welcome {.unnumbered}

<span id="visit-badge"></span>

<a href="https://anilyayavar.github.io/new-book/index.html"><img src="images/cover.jpg" alt="Cover of R for Audit Analytics" class="cover" width="705" height="1125"/></a>

This is the website of **R for Audit Analytics**, a book on data analytics for auditors, using the free and open-source R language. It is free to read, for everyone.

The book is written for auditors, in government and elsewhere, who want to analyse data themselves: to read the files an auditee gives them, clean and combine them, test them against rules, look for duplicates, gaps and unusual patterns, and turn the results into findings and reports. No knowledge of programming is assumed. Every technique is explained in plain language, and every one is shown at work on an audit problem, with Indian examples, amounts in lakh and crore, and the kind of data that auditors actually receive.

## What is in the book {.unnumbered}

The book has ten parts. The first three teach R and the essentials of handling and exploring data. The remaining seven are the audit toolkit.

| Part | What it covers |
|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| **I. R Basics** | The R language: objects, subsetting, functions, pipes, control statements, and functional programming |
| **II. Getting and Shaping Data** | Reading files, including PDFs and messy Excel; cleaning, merging, transforming, joining and reshaping data; dates; and data too large for Excel |
| **III. Exploring Data, Statistics and Sampling** | Charts, factors, descriptive statistics, probability, audit sampling, and statistical tests |
| **IV. Working with Strings** | Text manipulation, regular expressions, validating Indian identifiers like PAN, GSTIN and Aadhaar, and fuzzy matching of names |
| **V. Forensic Tests for Audit** | Rule-based validation, Benford's law, Nigrini's tests, duplicates, record linkage, gaps, and process mining |
| **VI. Patterns and Anomalies** | Regression, logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, PCA, clustering, association rules, time series, anomaly detection, and data envelopment analysis |
| **VII. Text Analytics** | Word frequencies, sentiment, and visualising text, applied to grievances and other free text |
| **VIII. Network Analytics** | Graphs and networks, and their use in finding related parties, circular trading and collusion |
| **IX. Geospatial Analytics** | Maps, geocoding and reverse geocoding, for checks on location |
| **X. Reporting** | Reproducible audit reports and Excel working papers, generated from code |

: The ten parts of the book {#tbl-parts}

The appendices list the datasets and the R packages used in the book, and explain the choice of colours for charts.

## How to read this book {.unnumbered}

- **New to R?** Start with *Gearing up*, which shows how to install R and RStudio, and then read Parts I to III in order. They build on one another. After that, the later parts can be read in any order.
- **Know some R already?** Skim Parts I and II for the audit examples and the newer features of the tidyverse, and go straight to the techniques you need.
- **Have a particular audit question?** Use the table below to find the chapter that answers it.

| If you want to... | See |
|------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| Read a bank statement or an order from a PDF, or an untidy Excel sheet | @sec-pdfxl |
| Work with data too big for Excel | @sec-duckdb |
| Check payments against rules, rates and limits | @sec-validate |
| Find payments made twice, or bills entered twice | @sec-dup |
| Find the same person in two lists, with no common ID | @sec-linkage |
| Find missing cheque or receipt numbers | @sec-gaps |
| Check whether a process was followed, step by step | @sec-process |
| Test whether amounts have been manipulated | @sec-benford, @sec-nigrini |
| Draw an audit sample, including monetary unit sampling | @sec-sampling |
| Decide whether a difference between offices is real or chance | @sec-tests |
| Rank cases by risk, to select them for examination | @sec-logistic, @sec-trees, @sec-forest |
| Find unusual records, months or units | @sec-anomaly |
| Compare the efficiency of hospitals, schools or offices | @sec-dea |
| Validate PAN, GSTIN, Aadhaar, IFSC, mobile numbers or email IDs | @sec-regex |
| Match names spelt differently | @sec-strsim |
| Find links between vendors, employees and accounts | @sec-netaudit |
| Analyse grievances or other text | @sec-text |
| Check addresses and locations on a map | @sec-geocoding |
| Produce a report for every district from one template | @sec-reports |

: Finding the right chapter {#tbl-findchapter}

## How the chapters are written {.unnumbered}

Most chapters follow the same plan, so that you always know where to look.

- **An audit problem** comes first, and the technique follows from it.
- **Data with planted cases.** Where real data cannot be shared, the chapter creates realistic data in R, and *plants* in it the irregularities to be found: a duplicate payment, a ghost employee, a tampered bank statement. The code that creates the data is folded away; click on it to see it. Every number quoted in the text is computed from the data, so the text and the results always agree.
- **Callouts** mark what matters most for audit:

::: callout-tip
## Audit tip
Practical advice from audit experience.
:::

::: callout-caution
Traps to avoid, and points where the method can mislead.
:::

- **A suggested workflow** near the end of each chapter lists the steps to follow on your own data, and a **Remember** box sums up the main ideas.
- **A summary of functions used** closes each chapter, as a quick reference.

## Software {.unnumbered}

The book uses R version 4.5 and the RStudio editor, both free. The code makes full use of the *tidyverse* family of packages, and of the native pipe `|>`. The packages used in each part, with a single command to install all of them, are listed in @sec-packages.

## A note on data {.unnumbered}

The author works for the Government of India. The opinions expressed in this book are personal to the author, and are not to be construed as those of the Government of India, or of the author in his official capacity. All datasets and examples in the book are either sample datasets available with R and its packages, open data available online, or data simulated by the author to demonstrate the case under discussion. All names of persons, firms, offices and places in the simulated data are made up. None of the datasets or examples pertains to any entity handled by the author in his official capacity, and nothing in the book breaches official secrecy in any manner.
